cells.tense: The weighing is steady just now, and no case has to be closed for it to hold.
cells.act: mark the end of it with a plain act
cells.ask: Give an old matter a plain, visible end: a box set outside, a note burned, a number entered once and the book shut.
cells.core:
Where the road ahead isn't visible yet and the next step is, you can feel what's fair without working the calculation. You give and take in a way that leaves no running total in either mouth, and nobody walks away owing more than simply next.

The next step is small and final: give an old matter a plain end. A box set outside, a note you burn, a number entered once and the book shut. None of it needs explaining. The end isn't a verdict on who was right before — it's where you stop reopening something that already happened. What is over gets to be over, and the free hand that comes back is free.

cells.tense: The reckoning is being run ahead of time, against a bill that hasn't come due.
cells.act: bear the next hour of it without deciding anything
cells.ask: Take what you're owed and carry it, undecided, for an hour. Don't forgive it, don't collect it, don't rule on it.
cells.core:
Fairness that flows is being pre-spent. You feel what's right, but you keep the ledger open in your head — who owes, who got more, what evens out. Silence starts to look like being shortchanged before anything has been settled.

Take what you're owed and carry it for an hour without deciding anything. Not forgiven, not collected, not forgotten. It will feel bigger than it is while you hold it; let it stay the size it actually is. You don't have to stop noticing it. You only stop ruling on it. The hour ends, nothing breaks, and the balance that was already there gets its turn.

cells.tense: A debt went uncollected, and the asking side of it is standing down.
cells.act: do the plain version first, before the plans
cells.ask: Do the plain version of a task you keep planning: the first simple step, today, ahead of any scheme. Badly is allowed.
cells.core:
Where things are set right, an imbalance sits visible and untouched. You can name it clearly and still let the asking go. Being treated unfairly stopped being something to move on.

Do the plain version of something you keep planning — the first simple step, done today, ahead of any scheme, badly if it has to be. Not the version where you confront anyone. Just the plain move, repeated. Repeating it is what keeps the light on. It won't argue your case in a room you don't control. It does something quieter: it keeps you from becoming the person who lets it stand. The plain step is enough for a day.
cells.sheetLine: One plain step today keeps the light on.

cells.tense: The tally is running without an author, and the pen is down.
cells.act: write the first thing you knew about it, before the reasons
cells.ask: Put down the first read you had on some unfairness you keep carrying, before you build the case for it. Leave it unargued.
cells.core:
The weighing happens in a room you aren't standing in. Notes get kept on who has and hasn't been fair — in a tone you wouldn't put in a message. You wouldn't call it a tally, and it doesn't need calling anything to be kept.

Put down the first read you had on some unfairness you keep carrying, before the reasons. The first read is usually quieter than the case you'd make for it. You don't have to act on it or defend it. Put it somewhere you can see it once. That's all a first line has to do, and it does more than the second one does.
cells.sheetLine: The first thing you saw is the one steering.
